title: Roles: project manager, project support and agile coach
blurb: Apply the guidance for the agile coach, project manager and project support: who handles which task, and who in a people list fits each role.
question: At Larkspur Rail, the finance director on the board wants a Gantt chart and a ten-page monthly report and is slowing agile adoption. Which role should work with him on this, and why?

teach.h: Three roles that keep the project moving
teach.body: The project manager runs the project day to day on the board's behalf, within agreed tolerances, as a servant leader between governance and the teams. Project support provides administration, tools advice and dashboard updates. The agile coach is a mentor and facilitator who helps the organization adopt and sustain agile, working across teams on systemic blockers and supporting the board, assurance and PM with expert knowledge.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 7.2, Table B.1

teach.h: Duties, and what is not their job
head: Role
Typical duties
Not their job
rows: Remove systemic blockers; coach leaders; embed agile ways of working
Day-to-day running within tolerances; agree work packages with POs; consult on backlogs and approaches; control risks
Admin for iterations and workshops; tools advice; update and pull dashboards; stakeholder analysis; lists

teach.h: The project manager as servant leader
teach.body: The PM has authority to run the project for the board within tolerances and constraints, and acts as a servant leader who links governance with the teams. Work is agreed with each product owner as a set of user stories; the PM consults POs and stakeholders on product backlogs and management approaches and makes sure risks are identified, assessed and controlled. The PM may attend daily stand-ups only with the delivery team's agreement.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 7.2, Table 12.1

steps.sub: Updates and pulls project and team dashboards

steps.label: Project dashboard
steps.sub: The board pulls what it needs

teach.caption: Project support also helps meet any stakeholder's reporting needs from the dashboards.

teach.h: The agile coach early in a change
teach.body: When an organization is new to agile, the coach starts by building knowledge and skills: theoretical training plus practical on-the-job coaching, tailored to the organization's own setting. Introducing tools first, lecturing on theory alone or coaching only some roles undermines the change. Later, the coach keeps working across teams on systemic blockers, such as a leader who resists dashboards.

root.label: A task or problem in the scenario

children.edge: Run day to day; agree work with POs
children.label: Project manager

teach.body: Agile coach Gita Bhatt works with assistant director Joan Whitaker, who does not want to be bothered with dashboards, and coaches project manager Simon Archer. Simon agrees each set of user stories with the digital team's product owner and joins stand-ups only when the team invites him. A project support officer from the project office updates the dashboards and pulls from them the written monthly report Joan wants, and helps with the stakeholder analysis.
teach.cite: Scenario AS4; book Table 7.2, Table B.1

teach.text: Do not confuse project support with project assurance: support does the administration and dashboards; assurance independently monitors adherence and cannot be provided by project support. And the agile coach works with the organization, not inside one team: that is the team coach.

items: Agile coach: organization-wide adoption, systemic blockers, coaching leaders and the PM.
PM: day-to-day running within tolerances; servant leader; agrees work packages with POs.
PM attends stand-ups with the team's agreement; does not prioritize across teams.
Project support: admin, tools, dashboards, stakeholder analysis, lists, communication flow.
Assurance must be independent of the PM, so project support cannot provide it.

summary: You can now apply the guidance for the agile coach, project manager and project support, and choose which of them should handle a task in a scenario. You can also pick the best person for each role from a people list.

A.q: Pinewick Home and Garden needs an agile coach to help the whole business adopt agile ways of working. Which person in the people list is best suited to the role?
options: Nikhil Rao, who has guided three areas into agile working
Fran Okonedo, Scrum master of the e-commerce delivery team
Patrick Dunne, project manager who joined from construction
Anita Shah, product manager who runs the e-commerce backlog
A.why: The agile coach helps the organization adopt and sustain agile and works across teams on systemic blockers (Table 7.2). Nikhil has already led adoption in several parts of the business.

whyNot.1: A Scrum master working with one team fits the team coach role.
whyNot.2: Patrick is the project manager, and he is new to agile himself.
whyNot.3: Managing one team's backlog fits the product owner role.

A.q: Callowmere's project manager needs someone to update the team and project dashboards, compile the list of students for the design panel and arrange the logistics of each workshop. Which role should do this?
options: Project assurance
Agile coach
Project support
Team coach
A.why: Project support provides administrative support tailored to iterations and workshops, updates and pulls information from dashboards and compiles lists (Table B.1).

whyNot.0: Assurance independently monitors adherence and advises; it is not administrative support.
whyNot.1: The agile coach supports adoption at organization level, not administration.
whyNot.3: The team coach helps one or two teams self-manage; dashboards and lists for the project are support's work.

A.q: At Saltmarsh, the service design team is ready for its next piece of work. Which role should agree the next set of user stories with the team's product owner, within the stage tolerances?
options: Chief product owner
Project manager
Project support
Agile coach
A.why: The project manager agrees work package descriptions, in agile a set of user stories, with each product owner within tolerances (7.3.1, Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: The CPO sets priorities across teams but does not authorize work packages.
whyNot.2: Project support helps with administration, not agreeing work.
whyNot.3: The agile coach advises on adoption; it does not agree work packages.

B.q: Larkspur's finance director, a board member, insists on a Gantt chart and a ten-page monthly report and questions why there is no fixed feature list. This is slowing the company's move to agile. Which role should work with him on this?
options: Team coach
Project support
Project assurance
Agile coach
B.why: The agile coach works across teams to identify and remove systemic blockers to agile adoption and supports the board with agile expertise (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: The team coach works within one or two delivery teams, not with board members.
whyNot.1: Support could produce the report he wants, but that would not address his resistance.
whyNot.2: Assurance monitors adherence; it does not coach leaders through adoption.

B.q: Pinewick's project manager wants to hear progress directly and plans to go to the e-commerce team's daily stand-ups. What should he do?
options: Join and run the stand-ups to speed them up
Attend them if the team agrees that he may
Ask the chief product owner to attend instead
Ask each developer for a written daily update
B.why: The project manager may attend daily stand-ups only with the delivery team's agreement (Table 12.1); otherwise he pulls progress from the team dashboard.

whyNot.0: Running the team's stand-up takes over its self-management.
whyNot.2: Sending the CPO does not respect the team's ownership of the event either.
whyNot.3: Written daily updates add reporting burden; progress is pulled from the team dashboard.

B.q: Easterholm's assistant director wants written monthly reports, while the teams keep team dashboards and a project dashboard. Which role should help meet her reporting needs by updating and pulling information from the dashboards?
options: Project support
Project assurance
Team coach
Chief product owner
B.why: Project support helps manage the reporting requirements of all stakeholders by updating and pulling information from project and team dashboards (Table B.1).

whyNot.1: Assurance advises on issues, risks and exceptions; it does not produce reports for stakeholders.
whyNot.2: The team coach supports the team's own ways of working.
whyNot.3: The CPO represents users and priorities, not reporting administration.

C.q: Easterholm has very little agile experience. Its new agile coach plans to begin by rolling out a dashboard tool to every team before any training or coaching takes place. Is this an appropriate application of the agile coach role, and why?
options: Yes, because dashboards make the work visible to leaders
Yes, because the coach helps embed agile ways of working
No, because people first need training and on-the-job coaching
No, because tools for the project are chosen by project support
C.why: Early in a change, people need theoretical training and practical on-the-job coaching tailored to their own setting; leaving them with a tool and no understanding undermines the change (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Visibility matters, but a tool without understanding does not build agile capability.
whyNot.1: True of the coach's role, but starting with a tool is not how to embed agile ways of working here.
whyNot.3: Project support advises on tools; that is not why the plan fails.

C.q: To satisfy Larkspur's finance director, the project manager allocates the app team's user stories to individual developers himself and tells them the order to work in. Is this an appropriate application of the project manager role, and why?
options: Yes, because the PM runs the project day to day for the board
Yes, because the finance director is a member of the board
No, because the chief product owner allocates the stories
No, because the PM agrees work with the PO, not developers
C.why: The PM is a servant leader who agrees work packages with the product owner as sets of user stories; the PO is the only role with direct authority over team members (7.3.1, Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: True, but the PM exercises day-to-day control through the PO, not by directing developers.
whyNot.1: A board member's wishes do not change the line of authority to the team.
whyNot.2: The CPO sets priorities across teams; it does not allocate stories to developers either.

C.q: To save money, Callowmere asks its project support officer, who works for the project manager and updates the dashboards, to provide project assurance as well. Is this appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because both roles give help to the project manager
Yes, because support already updates the dashboards
No, because assurance must be independent of the PM
No, because the agile coach provides project assurance
C.why: Project assurance must be independent of the project manager, so it cannot be provided by project support, which works for the PM (PRINCE2 role rules; Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: Assurance advises the board and PM, but its value comes from independence, which support lacks.
whyNot.1: Updating dashboards is support's admin work; it does not make the officer independent.
whyNot.3: The agile coach supports adoption; it is not the assurance role.

reteach.title: A touring theatre company
reteach.question: In a touring production, who is the coach, who is the stage manager and who keeps the paperwork?

blocks.body: The company manager runs the tour day to day within the producer's budget and dates, and agrees each week's work with the head of each crew: the project manager. The touring office keeps schedules, contact lists and the shared noticeboard up to date: project support. A consultant who helps the whole company adopt a new way of rehearsing, and works with the directors who resist it, is the agile coach.

head: On tour
Role
rows: Consultant changing how the company works

blocks.text: If the problem sits with leaders or the wider organization, think agile coach. If it is admin or dashboards, think project support.

explain.body: A mentor and facilitator for the organization: removes systemic blockers across teams, supports the board, assurance and PM with expert knowledge, and helps embed agile ways of working into the project's approaches.
explain.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 7.2, Table B.1

test.q: Which person at Easterholm County Council is best suited to the agile coach role?
options: Gita Bhatt, who led agile adoption in two councils
Oliver Grant, who runs sprint planning and retrospectives
Amy Fletcher, a senior user researcher in the team
Simon Archer, the project manager, new to agile
test.why: Gita has led agile adoption at organization level elsewhere, which fits the agile coach (Table 7.2).

whyNot.1: Running one team's sprint events fits the team coach role.
whyNot.2: User research is delivery work within the team.

explain.body: Runs the project day to day for the board within tolerances; servant leader linking governance and teams; agrees work packages with POs; consults POs and stakeholders on backlogs and management approaches; ensures risks are controlled.

test.q: Which of these is a responsibility of Callowmere's project manager?
options: Own the project backlog and its priorities
Agree work package descriptions with each PO
Approve the tolerances for agile decisions
Facilitate the web team's retrospectives
test.why: The PM agrees work package descriptions, as sets of user stories, with each product owner (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: The CPO owns the project backlog and cross-team priorities.
whyNot.2: The project executive approves tolerances for agile decision-making.
whyNot.3: Facilitating team workshops is a team coach task.

explain.body: Administrative support tailored to iterations and workshops; advice on tools; planning, risk and change management support; updating and pulling dashboards; help with stakeholder analysis; compiling lists; easing communication between governance and teams.
explain.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table B.1

test.q: Draycott's project manager needs help compiling the list of machines and fitting dates, updating the project dashboard and researching stakeholders for the stakeholder analysis. Which role should provide it?
options: Project assurance
Team coach
Tester
Project support
test.why: Project support compiles lists, updates dashboards and assists with stakeholder analysis (Table B.1).

whyNot.0: Assurance monitors and advises independently; it does not do this administration.
whyNot.1: The team coach supports team self-management.
whyNot.2: Testers check products against acceptance criteria and the DoD.

explain.body: The PM serves the teams and the board by linking them: making sure teams have what they need and the board gets the information it needs, rather than commanding team members.

test.q: Which behaviour shows Pinewick's project manager acting as a servant leader?
options: Assigning daily tasks to each developer
Setting priorities across both teams
Linking the board with the delivery teams
Approving the tolerances for the teams
test.why: The PM acts as a servant leader, facilitating collaboration between PRINCE2 Agile governance and the teams (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: Assigning tasks to developers bypasses the PO and the team's self-management.
whyNot.1: Cross-team priorities belong to the CPO.
